title: 2027 financial services predictions: Trusted data runs the bank
summary: What will 2027 bring for banks and insurers? Six predictions on AI agents, OSFI E-23 and EU AI Act deadlines, sovereign cloud, security, and AI ROI.
body_markdown:
My six financial services predictions for 2027 point to one conclusion: Banks and insurers will scale agentic AI only as fast as they can make their information trusted, governed, and explainable. It’s that time of year again, so I’ve dusted off my crystal ball. Fair warning: it’s the regulated kind, complete with an audit trail, a named owner, and a documented purpose, so if I’m wrong, at least we’ll know why.


Here’s what it’s showing me. For three years, banks and insurers treated generative AI like a very clever intern: great at summarizing, never trusted with the keys. In 2027, the intern gets promoted, and AI agents start doing real work in onboarding, lending, claims, payments, and compliance. Once software acts on a customer’s money, supervisors will want to know what data it used and what it did.


Here are my six predictions, and how we at OpenText are helping institutions get ready.


## 1. AI agents move into the back office, and document chaos becomes the bottleneck


*What will AI agents change in bank and insurer back offices in 2027?*


By the end of 2027, leading banks and insurers will run AI agents in production on at least one high-volume process, such as know your customer (KYC) and onboarding, underwriting, or claims intake. The hard part will be giving agents accurate, permissioned context from decades of scanned forms, policy documents, and correspondence.


Expect stalled agent projects that trace back to scattered content, duplicate customer records, and no clear data owner. Institutions that digitized and governed their content first will scale fastest.


**Where we fit:** One[large multinational bank](https://www.opentext.com/customers/multinational-bank) replaced paper-based KYC with automated capture and workflows on OpenText™ Content Management, OpenText™ Capture, and OpenText™ Process Automation. As OpenText CEO Ayman Antoun said when OpenText[announced its partnership with Cohere](https://www.opentext.com/about/press-releases/opentext-cohere-partner-to-combine-trusted-data-with-agentic-ai) , “Data is not the supporting act, it is what gives agentic AI the context it needs to perform.”


## 2. Model risk management expands to cover AI agents


*How will model risk management change for AI agents in 2027?*


In 2027, “who approved that?” will be asked about software as often as about people. Two deadlines show where the industry is heading:


**Jurisdiction** **Rule** **Effective date** **Who is affected**


**Canada** OSFI’s revised[Guideline E-23](https://www.osfi-bsif.gc.ca/en/guidance/guidance-library/guideline-e-23-model-risk-management-2027) on model risk management **May 1, 2027** All federally regulated financial institutions in Canada


**European Union** EU AI Act obligations for standalone high-risk systems, including credit scoring, as amended by the[Digital Omnibus on AI](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng) **December 2, 2027** Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems


I predict the model inventory will become the bank’s most important document. Agents that qualify as models will need an owner, a documented purpose, validated inputs, an audit trail, and an off switch.


**Where we fit:** Retention, lineage, and audit are what model risk teams will need for agents, and OpenText has delivered them for regulated financial content for more than three decades.


## 3. Sovereign cloud becomes the default for regulated financial data


*Why is sovereign cloud becoming the default for regulated financial data?*


In 2027, “where does this customer’s data live, and whose laws apply?” becomes a day-one question for every AI project. With supervisors focused on third-party and concentration risk, banks and insurers will keep their data, and the AI that touches it, within defined jurisdictions, with a credible exit plan.


This will favor partners who can run the same capabilities across public, sovereign, and private clouds, and on-premises where needed.


**Where we fit:** OpenText lets clients deploy in the cloud of their choice, including French and European sovereign cloud solutions with Google Cloud through its[partnership with S3NS](https://www.opentext.com/about/press-releases/opentext-and-s3ns-partner-to-deliver-european-sovereign-cloud-solutions) .


## 4. AI agents make identity governance a board-level issue


*How do banks secure AI agents and fight AI-driven fraud in 2027?*


AI agents expand the bank’s attack surface and make identity governance a board-level control issue. Agents could soon outnumber human users in many bank systems, and fraudsters will notice. I expect financial institutions to report more incidents in which manipulated or overprivileged agents contribute to payment fraud or data exposure.


Security teams will respond by treating every agent as an identity: least-privilege access, behavioral monitoring, and data-centric controls that follow sensitive information wherever it moves.


**Where we fit:**[OpenText research with the Ponemon Institute](https://www.opentext.com/about/press-releases/enterprises-rush-into-genai-without-security-foundations--new-ponemon-study-finds) found that 52% of enterprises have fully or partially deployed generative AI, but only 43% have adopted a risk-based AI governance approach. Closing that gap separates AI that fights fraud from AI that enables it.


## 5. Corporate banking competes on connected, agent-ready payment flows


*How will agentic AI change corporate banking and payments in 2027?*


In 2027, transaction banking becomes a prime place for AI agents, because the richest structured data already flows there: payment files, remittances, trade documents, and treasury messages. Agents will flag anomalies, map formats between counterparties, and clear payment exceptions in minutes, not days.


Corporate treasurers will start choosing banks on how easily they connect. Banks that plug into a client’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) system once, and let agents handle exceptions, will win wallet share.


**Where we fit:** OpenText™ Trading Grid™ already carries B2B transaction data at scale, and OpenText is[layering AI and agentic capabilities over it](https://blogs.opentext.com/power-whats-next-opentext-business-network-at-opentext-world-2026/) to help clients move toward autonomous operations.


## 6. The AI ROI reckoning arrives, and institutions consolidate


*Which AI projects will survive the 2027 return-on-investment reckoning?*


In 2027, CFOs will stop funding AI pilots that cannot show a number: cost per onboarded customer, days to settle a claim, false positives cut. Many proofs of concept will be quietly retired.


The survivors will sit inside existing workflows, run on governed content, and come from a short list of platforms the institution already trusts. Expect vendor consolidation.


**Where we fit:**[19 of the top 20 financial services and insurance companies](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/industry/banking) use OpenText. That installed base of trusted, governed content is where practical, measurable AI gets built.


## What this means for financial services leaders


Every prediction comes back to the point I make in nearly every client meeting: in 2027, a financial institution’s AI will only be as trustworthy as its information. Agents need clean, current content. Supervisors need lineage and audit trails.


Three things worth doing before the year starts:


1. **Inventory your agents now.** Determine which AI agents qualify as models under E-23, then assign ownership, document their intended use and inputs, and apply controls proportionate to risk.
2. **Fix the content before scaling the AI.** Pick one high-volume process, such as onboarding or claims, and get its documents digitized, classified, and governed end to end.
3. **Choose platforms built for regulated data.** Favor partners who can run where your regulators need you to run, and who can show measurable results.


At OpenText, this is the ground we have stood on for more than three decades. In 2027, it decides which institutions can put AI to work safely, and which are left explaining themselves to their regulators.


That’s all the crystal ball is showing me for now. I’ll be back next November to mark my own homework, audit trail and all. In the meantime, I’d love to hear what your crystal ball is telling you.
